```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(width = 110)
library(sciparseR)
```

## Batches with a cache

`sc_parse_batch()` parses many files, keeps going when one fails and
records why. With a cache directory, each result is stored under a key
built from the SHA-256 of the file, the configuration hash, the package,
schema and pdftools versions. A file is parsed again only when one of
these changes; renaming or moving a file does not invalidate the cache,
and a cache hit points to the file's current path and name. An entry
that cannot be read is parsed again and replaced.

```{r}
files <- system.file("extdata", c("single_column.pdf", "two_column.pdf", "trial_tables.pdf",
                                   "trial_article.xml"), package = "sciparseR")
files <- c(files, file.path(tempdir(), "not-there.pdf"))
cache <- file.path(tempdir(), "sciparseR-cache")

b <- sc_parse_batch(files, cache_dir = cache)
b
b$status[, c("file", "status", "cached", "seconds", "n_warnings", "error")]

b2 <- sc_parse_batch(files[1:4], cache_dir = cache)
b2$status[, c("file", "cached", "seconds")]
sc_cache_info(cache)[, c("source", "doc_id", "package_version", "size_bytes")]
```

`workers` runs files in parallel with forked processes on Unix-alike
systems. Cache entries are written to a temporary file and renamed, so an
interrupted run never leaves a half written entry.

A typical batch workflow continues with extraction and validation:

```{r}
docs <- Filter(Negate(is.null), b$documents)
ext <- lapply(docs, function(d) sc_validate(sc_extract(d, "clinical_trial")))
summary_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ext), function(n) {
  r <- ext[[n]]$records
  data.frame(file = n, records = nrow(r),
             fails = sum(ext[[n]]$validation$result == "fail"),
             to_review = nrow(sc_review_queue(ext[[n]])))
}))
summary_tab
```

## Export formats

| Function | Content | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `sc_export_json()` / `sc_read_json()` | full document or extraction, versioned | archiving, exchange, other languages |
| `sc_export_markdown()` | readable text with pipe tables | reading, LLM context, notes |
| `sc_export_csv()` | one CSV per entity table | spreadsheets |
| `sc_export_parquet()` | one Parquet file per entity table | data pipelines (needs arrow) |
| `sc_export_jats()` | JATS XML built from the model | XML tooling, round trips |
| `sc_export_evidence()` | records joined with evidence | review, audit trails of extraction |
| `sc_export_tables()` | one CSV per table plus long cell table | table reuse |

```{r}
doc <- docs[["trial_tables.pdf"]]
x <- ext[["trial_tables.pdf"]]
out <- file.path(tempdir(), "export")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

### JSON

The JSON file holds every entity table and the provenance lists. The
absolute path of the source is left out unless `include_path = TRUE`; the
file name and checksum are always there. Reading it back restores the
column types of every table and the types of the metadata fields. A
document read back without its path cannot be highlighted or cropped
until `doc$source$path` is set to the PDF file.

```{r}
f <- sc_export_json(doc, file.path(out, "doc.json"))
d2 <- sc_read_json(f)
all(vapply(c("blocks", "cells", "tables"), function(e) identical(d2[[e]], doc[[e]]), logical(1)))
```

The JSON Schema of both object types ships with the package:

```{r}
list.files(system.file("schema", package = "sciparseR"))
```

### Markdown

```{r}
md <- sc_export_markdown(doc, file.path(out, "doc.md"))
cat(readLines(md), sep = "\n")
```

### JATS

```{r}
jf <- sc_export_jats(doc, file.path(out, "doc.xml"))
back <- sc_parse(jf, format = "jats")
sc_table_to_dataframe(back, back$tables$table_id[1])
```

### Evidence, CSV and Parquet

```{r}
e <- read.csv(sc_export_evidence(x, file.path(out, "evidence.csv")))
e[1:3, c("field", "value", "status", "evidence_page", "evidence_char_start", "evidence_char_end")]
basename(sc_export_csv(x, file.path(out, "csv")))
if (requireNamespace("arrow", quietly = TRUE)) basename(sc_export_parquet(doc, file.path(out, "parquet")))
```
